convention: The same three-state convention as messages/lg.needs-translation.json, for the Patients namespace: every leaf key in Patients.lg.json is either translated (its value differs from the English one), awaiting a translator (it holds the English text verbatim and its dotted path is listed below), or identical on purpose. src/i18n/i18n.test.ts checks only the BASE catalogues, so nothing enforces this file; it is a worklist for a translator, not a gate. What IS enforced is that both catalogues hold the same keys — src/i18n/messages.ts proves it with a bidirectional `satisfies` at compile time.
whyMostOfItIsStillEnglish: The agent that wrote this namespace does not speak Luganda. This is the consent screen, and a confident-sounding wrong translation here is not a cosmetic defect: consent obtained from wording the patient did not understand is not consent, and the record would nonetheless carry a hash proving they were shown it. An honest English string a reader can recognise as foreign and ask about is the safer failure. Only short, unambiguous field labels were translated. NOTE that the POLICY TEXT ITSELF IS NOT IN THIS FILE and never will be: it is real Luganda prose written by the party legally answerable for it and served by GET /v1/consent-policies/current, and the screen renders it verbatim in the reader's language. The backend's own docblock says that rendering is a working translation awaiting a native-speaker review before this policy version ships to patients — that review is the higher priority of the two.
translateFirst: Patients.consent.agree, Patients.consent.decline, Patients.consent.declineButton, Patients.consent.declineHeading, Patients.consent.declineBody and Patients.consent.declineStillWelcome. Those six are the affirmative action itself and the way out of it — the words a patient presses are the consent, and they sit beside a policy the API already serves in Luganda. Then Patients.consent.telemedicineLocked and Patients.consent.deliveryBody, which explain why a question is closed and why one is missing. Then Patients.history.withdrawDoesNotDelete and Patients.history.withdrawStops, which must not be translated into a promise of deletion the clinic cannot lawfully perform.
identicalOnPurposeNote: Both label a <details> that opens into the OTHER language, and each is deliberately written in the language it opens into — so a Luganda reader on an English page recognises the way in, and the summary is marked with a matching lang attribute for a screen reader. Translating either one would defeat the thing it is for.
